description: What if the power went out tonight, and stayed out for a month? 🕯️ Most of us have lost the everyday know-how our grandparents relied on without a second thought, the kind of quiet, practical skill that once kept a household fed, warm, and running smoothly no matter what happened outside. This book hands that knowledge back to you, not as a doomsday manual, but as a genuinely useful guide to living with more independence, less waste, and real confidence in your own two hands. Inside, you will learn how to: Preserve a season's harvest through canning, root cellaring, smoking, dehydrating, and fermenting, so nothing goes to waste and your pantry lasts all winter Build genuine self sufficiency at home with soap and candle making, natural cleaning remedies, basic tool repair, and simple animal husbandry for chickens and goats Set up reliable off grid systems, including water sourcing and purification, wood stove heating, solar power basics, and traditional oil lamp lighting Master core wilderness survival skills like shelter building, fire starting without matches, safe foraging principles, and navigation without GPS Prepare your whole family with practical, calm, step by step guidance on emergency planning, 72 hour kits, and passing these skills down to the next generation 🌾 Written in clear, practical language and organized so you can jump straight to what you need, this is the guide for anyone who wants to rely a little less on the grid and a little more on themselves. Whether you are new to homesteading, prepping for emergencies, or simply curious about the skills your grandparents took for granted, this book gives you the tools to bring them back into your own home. title: Mini Farming: Self-Sufficiency on 1/4 Acre

description: Build a more capable, resilient life—one practical system at a time. Homesteading does not require a remote farm, complete independence, or an overnight change of lifestyle. It begins with useful skills, informed decisions, and projects you can sustain. Practical Homesteading is a comprehensive guide to growing food, managing essential resources, preserving a harvest, maintaining tools and infrastructure, and developing greater everyday self-reliance. Whether you live in an apartment, a suburban home, or on rural land, this book will help you choose realistic projects and adapt them to your space, climate, budget, and available time. Inside, you will learn how to: Assess a property, balcony, backyard, or growing space Create a realistic first-year homesteading plan Set priorities, estimate costs, and avoid expanding too quickly Improve soil and plan crops around meals and household needs Start seeds, propagate plants, and establish perennial crops Calculate water requirements and prepare for dry periods Understand household energy loads and evaluate renewable systems Decide whether keeping chickens, goats, bees, or other animals is appropriate Preserve food through drying, freezing, fermenting, canning, and suitable storage Organize tools, maintenance, repairs, and seasonal work Cook more effectively from the garden, pantry, and preserved harvest Build local networks for shared knowledge, equipment, and resilience The book also includes crop-planning cards, decision tables, water and energy worksheets, maintenance records, seasonal checklists, and practical tools for turning broad ambitions into manageable actions. title: Back to Basics: A Complete Guide to Traditional Skills (Back to Basics Guides)
description: Over 1,500,000 copies sold—an international bestseller! NATIONAL BESTSELLER! #4 BALTIMORE SUN BESTSELLER #7 AMAZON WEEKLY BESTSELLER Fully updated—Dye your own wool, raise chickens, make your own cheddar cheese, build a log cabin, and much much more. Anyone who wants to learn basic living skills—the kind employed by our forefathers—and adapt them for a better life in the twenty-first century need look no further than this eminently useful, full-color guide. Countless readers have turned to Back to Basics for inspiration and instruction, escaping to an era before power saws and fast-food restaurants and rediscovering the pleasures and challenges of a healthier, greener, and more self-sufficient lifestyle. Now newly updated, the hundreds of projects, step-by-step sequences, photographs, charts, and illustrations in Back to Basics will help you dye your own wool with plant pigments, graft trees, raise chickens, craft a hutch table with hand tools, and make treats such as blueberry peach jam and cheddar cheese. The truly ambitious will find instructions on how to build a log cabin or an adobe brick homestead. More than just practical advice, this is also a book for dreamers—even if you live in a city apartment, you will find your imagination sparked, and there’s no reason why you can’t, for example, make a loom and weave a rag rug. title: Lost Timeless Skills of Independence: 180 Illustrated Old-Fashioned Skills and 48 Hands-On
description: Make more. Mend more. Put practical independence within reach. A torn bag. A loose cabinet pull. A harvest that needs storing. These everyday moments are opportunities to become more capable—and make better use of what you already have. Lost Timeless Skills of Independence by David L. Owens brings together 180 illustrated skills, including 48 expanded hands-on projects , to help you build useful habits around your home, kitchen, garden, and workshop. You don’t need acres of land or a fully equipped workshop to begin. Start with a manageable task, follow the instructions, and build your confidence through practice. Inside, you’ll discover how to: Use and care for everyday tools: measure accurately, secure your work, organize hardware, and recognize when equipment needs attention. Grow food in the space you have: start seedlings, plant container herbs, build a simple pea trellis, and improve your gardening routine. Preserve and organize food: prepare freezer portions, rotate pantry supplies, keep useful batch records, and find tested preservation guidance. Develop traditional kitchen skills: make flatbreads, shake cream into butter, prepare simple dressings, and turn sound leftover bread into useful crumbs. Repair, mend, and reuse: patch a cloth bag, replace a button, renew weatherstripping, and give worn household materials another purpose. Prepare for interruptions and reduce waste: organize emergency water supplies, test battery lighting, compare unit prices, and make informed repair-or-replace decisions. Detailed black-and-white engraving-style illustrations accompany the instruction.
